minutes.headline: Task force agreed to include regional districts as comps despite worse results, and to start with revenue next meeting.
minutes.summary: The Budget Task Force reviewed comparable towns and school districts for town and school analysis, discussing whether to compare to similar towns or to competitors for employees (including regional districts). Members agreed to include regionals with a qualifier. They also debated how to sort obligatory, essential and discretionary costs, and set the schedule so revenue comes first, with obligatory expenses next.

attendees.role: presenter (town comps; stated this is her last meeting)

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comments on last week's meeting; none was apparent.
Chair assumed there were no public comments at close since no one else was attending.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member asked why Ayer showed a very large enterprise revenue figure; Heather said it likely reflects town enterprise funds and she would need more research.
Members discussed the CPA surcharge and state match as a possible revenue source Lunenburg has not adopted; the state match has declined over time.
Debt service is high as a percentage of the operating budget on the comparison chart, which Heather called a weakness as a financial indicator and why she avoided borrowing.
Including regional districts makes Lunenburg look worse on pay and retention; regionals get state funds such as busing that single towns cannot.
Asked whether the override would improve the comparison; the data shown lags and wouldn't be comparable yet.
Without the override, Lunenburg would be at the lowest end of the comparison list of school budgets.
Contracting consultants for speech-language and similar services costs two or three times more than employing staff.
No change from the Friday meeting; legislation would be needed to change the funding formula.

budget_items.topic: Cherry sheet and DLS revenue categories
budget_items.what_was_said: DLS data back to FY21 includes Chapter 70, school transportation, charter tuition reimbursement, school lunch and school choice.
Group agreed to look back about ten years on revenue where available; school budgets go back to 2009 but grant and fee revenue may not.

decisions.decision: Include regional school districts as comps, with a qualifier labeling which are regional; Heather saw no issue with it.
School-side comps considered settled with regionals included; town list to be refined from the union of Evan's and Heather's lists.
Start with revenue at the next meeting and work backward; obligatory expenses, kept non-granular, follow in the meeting after.
Town side will gather revenue history back ten years where possible for a master revenue document.
Hope that the Capital Planning Committee's five-year plan can be handed off at the September 30th meeting.

what_happened.line: The Budget Task Force agreed by consensus to include regional school districts as comparison peers, with a qualifier marking which are regional.
School-side comparisons were treated as settled, and the town-side list is to be refined from the union of two members' lists.
The group set the order of work: revenue at the next meeting, then obligatory expenses kept non-granular in the meeting after.
The town side will gather revenue history back about ten years, where available, into a master revenue document.
No votes were taken. Members noted that adding regionals makes Lunenburg look worse on teacher pay and retention.

why_it_matters: The peer group chosen here sets the yardstick for later judgements on school spending, pay and the override, so the choice to include regionals shapes how Lunenburg's budget will be described.
Revenue, including state aid and local receipts, will be examined before costs, so the task force's view of what the town can raise will come before any discussion of what to cut.
